title: Exceptions for Control Flow
pattern: Relying on panic handling or try-catch blocks to catch predictable errors that could be checked up front with a simple conditional statement.
why_bad: Exceptions are expensive and disrupt the normal execution flow, creating tangled "spaghetti code" that is difficult to read, maintain, and test [28:430].
detection: Using try-catch blocks or panic catches for index-out-of-bounds, null pointer checks, or simple parsing tasks that have obvious guard tests [28:430].
fix: Replace exception-throwing pathways with predictive guard statements [28:430].
